summary: Sudden latency and tail-time spike in dedicated pool following tenant preemption/eviction events
description: Issue summary: Since ~2026-03-10T14:30Z, NimbleAI has reported a sharp increase in median and p99 latency for requests routed to their dedicated GPU pool. The spike correlates with a series of preemptive eviction events and rapid tenant slot reassignments triggered by autoscaler activity. Impact: Customer-facing API calls experienced 5–12x higher p99 tail latency for ~40 minutes; several streaming sessions disconnected mid-stream. This is impacting production throughput and user-facing SLAs. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated-az-usw2-03), prod traffic, region us-west-2. Steps observed/repro: 1) High short-lived burst from tenant A caused scheduler to preempt idle slots and reassign GPUs. 2) Eviction sequence triggered slot draining and KV-cache invalidations. 3) Tenants B and C received sudden allocation changes causing KV cache misses and rewarm overhead. 4) Requests experienced elevated token generation times and streaming disconnects. Observed behaviour: - p50 increased from ~80ms to ~450ms, p99 from ~320ms to ~3.2s. - Autoscaler logs show a flurry of preemption operations and immediate re-alloc attempts. - GPU utilization shows hotspots on a subset of nodes while others sit underutilized. - Eviction events include preemption_reason: "policy-burst" in scheduler logs. Expected behaviour: Autoscaler/scheduler should smooth transitions, avoid mass simultaneous preemptions, and maintain KV cache warm paths to prevent full rewarm for colocated tenants. Initial mitigation applied: 1) Support temporarily raised eviction cooldown for NimbleAI's pool to reduce churn. 2) Forced routing of high-latency requests to a compatible fallback model version (lower-memory) for the worst-affecting routes. 3) Notified on-call infra team and placed watch on autoscaler tunables.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 14:28Z spike seen on customer dashboard. 14:30Z multiple preemption events; scheduler trace shows batch of 12 preemptions in <90s. Hypotheses: 1) Aggressive autoscaler policy (burst scaling + immediate preemption) caused coordinated slot reassignments. 2) KV-cache invalidation on reassign causes rewarm penalty for chat workloads with long context. 3) Underlying placement bin-packing introduced GPU pinning that amplified noisy-tenant effects. Evidence: - Scheduler debug trace (trace_id: trace-20260310-14-30) shows concurrent EvictTask for tenants A/C/D. - Serving runtime logs show repeated KV cache misses and full session reinitialization for affected model sessions. - Node metrics show GPU memory fragmentation on nodes with high eviction counts. Actions taken: - Collected full scheduler traces and node-level logs; uploaded to S3 bucket nimbleai-incident-20260310 (link in Confluence). - Throttled preemption loop (hotfix branch referenced in PR 3245). - Eng running simulation to reproduce preemption order edge case. Open questions: whether packer/placer heuristics should favor cache affinity over tight bin packing for dedicated pools.

steps_to_reproduce: 1) Recreate tenant burst profile using load-tester against dedicated-az-usw2-03 with simultaneous start of 100 short streams and 40 long-context chat sessions. 2) Apply autoscaler policy matching customer prod config (policy: burst_scale=true, preemption_cooldown=30s). 3) Observe scheduler trace and serving runtime KV cache behavior during scale events. 4) Verify p99 latency on token generation and count of session reinitializations.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:00 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial triage complete; raised to P1 due to SLA impact. Added temporary eviction cooldown for the pool and routed critical traffic to fallback model. Notified infra on-call.
2026-03-10 15:22 - Marcus Lin (On-call SRE): Found batch of 12 concurrent EvictTasks in scheduler logs. Investigating scheduler release ordering. Opening a hotfix to gate preemption concurrency.
2026-03-10 16:05 - Priya Rao (Serving Runtime): Confirmed KVCache misses and full rewarm for affected sessions. Adding metric to track rewarm duration per session.
2026-03-10 17:10 - Support (Aisha): Customer reports partial recovery after eviction cooldown; still seeing intermittent p99 spikes. Working with Eng to validate hotfix impact.
2026-03-11 09:40 - Marcus Lin: Hotfix PR #3245 applied to canary group; no regressions observed. Preparing rollout and config change plan to favor cache-affinity during placement for dedicated pools.
2026-03-12 11:00 - Customer (NimbleAI, Ops): Thank you — we saw improved stability after the changes. Asking for follow-up on placement heuristics and SLA credits discussion.
resolution: Mitigation performed: Increased eviction cooldown for affected dedicated pool, applied hotfix to limit concurrent preemptions (PR 3245), and temporarily routed heavy chat sessions to a fallback model to avoid rewarm penalty. Post-incident actions: 1) Engineering to implement placement heuristic change favoring KV-cache affinity for dedicated pools (RFC opened, Confluence link provided). 2) Add automated alerting for >5 preemptions within 2m for a single pool. 3) Follow up with NimbleAI on SLA remediation and a recommended configuration bundle for their dedicated pool. Ticket remains open pending placement-heuristic PR and SLA follow-up.
next_steps: 1) Implement packer change to prefer cache-affinity (owner: Priya Rao, target branch: feature/cache-affinity). 2) Roll out preemption concurrency guard cluster-wide (owner: Marcus Lin, target date: 2026-03-18). 3) Validate with NimbleAI QA load test after changes. 4) Postmortem to be drafted and linked in Confluence.
